topic: The Mathematical Trinity: Powers, Roots, and Logarithms

sections.title: Introduction: The Three Perspectives of a Number
lecture_lines: Powers, roots, and logs are three perspectives.
They describe the same relationship: base, exponent, result.
Think of this as a triangle of operations.
animations: Display the title 'Three Perspectives of a Number' in #FFFFFF color.
Fade in three distinct [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/triangle.svg] nodes representing 'Power', 'Root', and 'Log' in #FF6600, #33CC33, and #3399FF respectively.
Animate connecting lines between these three nodes to show their interrelation.

sections.title: Prerequisite: The Exponential Foundation
lecture_lines: The base is our starting unit.
The exponent is our growth intensity.
The result is our final total.
animations: Display the expression 'b^x = y' in #FFFFFF color [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/none.svg].
Highlight the variable 'b' (base) in #FF6600 and animate a pulsing effect [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/none.svg].
Highlight the variable 'x' (exponent) in #FFFF00 and animate a pulsing effect [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/none.svg].

sections.title: The First Twist: Roots as Inverse Powers
lecture_lines: Roots help us find the base.
Think of roots as undoing exponents.
If two cubed is eight, cube-root eight is two.
animations: Display 'y^(1/n) = x' in #FFFFFF color using [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/cube.svg] as a visual anchor.
Morph the previous power equation into this root form.
Show a 'swap' animation of 'x' and 'n' to highlight the inverse relationship using [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/cube.svg] to represent the transformation space.

sections.title: The Final Twist: Logarithms as Time-Keepers
lecture_lines: Logs help us find the exponent.
How many doubles to reach eight? Three.
animations: Color the 'log' operator in #3399FF to match the 'Log' node from section 1.
Animate the transition of 'b' and 'y' into the logarithm notation, incorporating the [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/clock.svg] to signify the timing of the transformation.

sections.title: Summary and Connection: The Universal Equation
lecture_lines: Shift your focus to find the unknown.
animations: Display all three forms together on screen in a triangle arrangement, centered around [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/none.svg].
Flash each equation sequentially in their respective colors.
Connect all three with a central cycle arrow to represent the universal equation flow.
